analyst.summary: ITC Hotels' Q1 FY27 results (16 July 2026, two days before this review and after the apparent quant data cutoff) show accelerating fundamentals - 36% PAT growth, 8% RevPAR growth with a 33% industry premium, 35% management-fee growth as the asset-light managed portfolio crosses 200 hotels - even as the stock is down ~33% from its 52-week high, which reads as a post-listing valuation de-rating rather than a business breakdown. The India luxury-hotel upcycle (demand CAGR outrunning supply by ~5 points through FY28) still has genuine multi-year runway, FY26 earnings quality was clean (the one-off was a conservative expense, not an inflating gain), and the balance sheet is debt-free/net-cash. At ~44-46x trailing for a 7% ROE the stock is not cheap, sits mid-pack against peers (IHCL 54-67x, EIH/Chalet 27-33x), and carries a standing (if unconfirmed) overhang from ITC Limited's retained 40% stake plus some capital-allocation noise from owned-asset bolt-on M&A. Hold: the fresher print argues against selling into what looks like an operating inflection, but this is not a cheap add-more situation either.
